_comment: Golden test vectors live here. See docs/03-specifications.md §6.4.

generation.method: Every *.json vector file in this directory (aside from this README) was produced by a throwaway Swift script run once via `swift <script>.swift` (CryptoKit on macOS, same as spec §6.4's Scripts/gen-vectors.swift), then hand-copied into JSON. The tests in this target re-run the same AirMouseCrypto APIs against the frozen inputs and assert byte-exact equality with the frozen outputs, so a future regression in HKDF/AEAD/HMAC wiring is caught even though the vector generator itself is not checked in (see 'deviation' below for why).
generation.hkdf_aead_vector.json: Inputs are exactly spec §6.4's 'AEAD framing' vector: secret = 0x00..0x1F (32 bytes counting up), sessionID = 0x0A0B0C0D, direction c2h, counter = 7. kC2H/kH2C/nonce/AAD/ciphertext/tag/datagram were computed by calling CryptoKit's HKDF<SHA256> and ChaChaPoly directly (not via this module, to keep the vector independent of the implementation under test) with those inputs, plus the fixed 16-byte plaintext payload spec §6.4 gives for its 'Motion payload' vector.
generation.pairing_proof_vector.json: Inputs are arbitrary-but-fixed byte sequences (S = 0xA0..0xAF, exporter = 0x00..0x1F, nonce = 0x40..0x4F, clientFP/hostFP/hostID as documented inline) chosen only to be distinct and non-degenerate; spec §6.4 does not fix specific byte values for this vector ('fixed S, exporter, nonce, FPs, hostID → expected proof and hostProof hex'), so this file supplies its own concrete numbers. proof/hostProof were computed via CryptoKit's HMAC<SHA256> directly. The negative vector flips the first byte of hostID and records the resulting (different) proof.
generation.replay_window_vector.json: Sequence is exactly spec §6.4's replay-window vector: [0,1,2,1,70,5,6,70,200,136,135]. THE PATTERN DIFFERS FROM THE SPEC'S PRINTED TABLE — see 'deviation' below. The frozen pattern here was produced by hand-tracing spec §3.5.4's own pseudocode against this sequence, which was then cross-checked with a standalone Swift reimplementation of that same pseudocode (kept only in scratch, not checked in, since it exists solely to double-check arithmetic and is not itself a vector generator worth freezing).

deviation.what: docs/03-specifications.md §6.4 prints the replay-window accept/reject pattern as [A,A,A,R,A,R,A,R,A,A,R] for sequence [0,1,2,1,70,5,6,70,200,136,135]. Running §3.5.4's own algorithm on that sequence — 'elif highest − counter ≥ 64: drop (too old)' — instead produces [A,A,A,R,A,R,R,R,A,R,R]: the values 6 (position 7, distance 70−6=64) and 136 (position 10, distance 200−136=64) are BOTH rejected as too-old, not accepted.
deviation.why_the_algorithm_wins: §6.4's own prose for this vector explicitly says '5 and 6 are ≥ 64 behind 70 ... rejected' and '136 is exactly 64 behind 200 → rejected', which only matches the [..,R,R,..]/[..,R,R] outcome, not the printed letter array (which shows 'A' at both of those positions). The prose and the printed array in §6.4 contradict each other, and the printed array also contradicts §3.5.4's algorithm text. Given CLAUDE.md's 'never contradict the spec' instruction cannot be honored toward all three sources simultaneously, this implementation follows §3.5.4 (the algorithm definition, which is unambiguous and is what the type is actually specified to implement) and §6.4's own prose (which independently corroborates the algorithm's result), and treats the printed letter array in §6.4 as a transcription error to be fixed at the spec source.
deviation.action_requested: Flagged in the AirMouseCrypto delivery report for spec maintainers; docs/03-specifications.md §6.4 was not edited by this module (out of scope: docs/0*.md is owned by other agents).
